items.E1: FLEX (PSI-69): Flame Extinguishment Experiment. Flight investigation, platform: International Space Station (ISS); hardware: MDCA droplet rig · CIR.
items.E2: Objective, from NASA PSI: The FLEX (Flame Extinguishment Experiment) investigation aims to map the flammability limits of liquid fuels in microgravity environments, measure the effectiveness of various gaseous fire suppressants such as CO2, He, and SF6, and develop reliable predictive models for combustion limits under reduced gravity conditions. The mission seeks to validate and improve simplified models by incorporating detailed chemical reactions, heat transfer, and material movement, using both space-based data and extensive ground-based tests.
items.E3: 274 records in its PSI experimental tables, 274 with a labeled outcome.
items.E4: Conditions tested: 12%–34% O2, 0.69–3.05 atm.
items.E5: Varied: Fuel, Ambient pressure; mmHg, O2 initial ambient composition; mole fraction, N initial ambient composition; mole fraction, CO2 initial ambient composition; mole fraction, He initial ambient composition; mole fraction. Measured: Visible flame extinction diameter; mm, Burning rate; mm, Test end.
items.E6: Relevance score out of 100 by habitat: cabin 99.7, EVA prep 99.2, lunar base 95.1, exploration atmosphere 82.3, spacesuit 49.7. Rank 1 of 24 for the lunar base.
items.E7: Benefit on Earth, from NASA PSI: The research impacts and Earth benefits of the FLEX mission are significant and multifaceted. By enhancing our understanding of microgravity combustion, the mission directly contributes to improved fire safety protocols for future space missions, ensuring the safety of crew members in environments where traditional fire suppression methods may be ineffective.
items.E8: Most similar investigations (similarity 0 to 1): CFI (0.58) and FLEX-2 (0.44).
items.E9: Layers of fire safety it informs: Suppression, Prevention. Publications listed in PSI: 51.

items.E2: Objective, from NASA PSI: The BRE flight program seeks to establish the burning conditions in a quiescent microgravity ambient in terms of material properties. The specific flight objectives are as follows. 1. Observe burning behavior in long-duration microgravity for CH4/N2 and C2H4/N2mixtures on porous circular burners of 25 and 50 mm diameter.

items.E2: Objective, from NASA PSI: The two main objectives for BASS are to: 1.) The relation between these can be investigated by observing flames burning for the longer times available in flight.

items.E6: Pressurized rover (30% O2, 10.2 psi, 9 m³): methanol droplet fire goes out on its own 8% (90% range 1–16%); one rod burn adds about 1.64 ppm of CO once mixed.
items.E7: Flight test the data asks for: Flammability limits of habitat materials (fabric, PMMA, Nomex) at ≥30% O2 and ≤10.2 psi. Why: NASA PSI's tables hold no solid burned above 22.7% O2 or at reduced pressure. Saffire V and VI (published, not in PSI) burned 4 samples at 26.2–31.0% O2, all at one airflow and with no limit mapped, so every materials limit for the base is still extrapolated.
items.E8: Flight test the data asks for: Methanol droplet at 28% O2, 0.75 atm, 30% CO2. Why: Where the 200 models disagree most near lunar-base air (90% range 11–48%).
items.E9: Flight test the data asks for: Any flame at lunar gravity (0.17 g). Why: PSI holds microgravity and 1 g data only; partial-gravity facilities (LUCI, FM2) have no data in PSI yet.
